title: GPU IRQ coalescing & scheduler interaction — investigation notes and hotfix validation
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the investigation into intermittent tail-latency spikes observed on a subset of inference nodes running quantized Llama-variant models (q4_0) between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-11. Symptoms: SLO misses (99th pctl crossing 350ms target), customer escalations for 'stuttered' streaming responses, and increased variance in per-request service time. Impact was isolated to ~12% of GPU-backed workers in prod-us-west-2, primarily on instance type g7x-large (8x A100s) with mixed tenant traffic.

Why this doc is different: previous postmortems focus on scheduler batching/backpressure and kV cache repop storms. This investigation discovered a cross-layer interaction between host NIC interrupt coalescing, the Linux scheduler's softirq handling, and our GPU runtime's batch flush timing — producing short (~20-200ms) stalls that amplified tail latency for streaming/low-qps traces.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-01-09 03:10 UTC — First alert: 99p spikes on model:llama-q4-prod-route-7 (Grafana INF alert).
- 2026-01-09 03:12 UTC — Support ticket from customer A describing jitter during multi-chunk streams.
- 2026-01-09 03:30-06:00 UTC — On-call runbook checks (node restarts, evicting drain) temporarily reduced noise.
- 2026-01-10 10:00 UTC — Eng-serving-runtime triage; reproduced locally in staging with controlled traffic.
- 2026-01-11 14:00 UTC — Profiling (perf, ftrace, nvtx, nvidia-smi dmon) shows 10-150ms idle gaps in the GPU kernel loop coincident with bursts of softirq processing on host.
- 2026-01-12 09:00 UTC — Hotfix candidate rolled to canary: adjust NIC interrupt coalescing and add scheduler-affinity hint to runtime IO threads.
- 2026-01-13 02:00 UTC — Canary validation: 99p reduced from 420ms -> 210ms on canary nodes under synthetic low-qps streaming workload.
- 2026-01-18 16:30 UTC — Global rollout with mitigations; longer-term follow-ups scheduled.

Observed signals / evidence:
- Grafana: 99p spikes correlated with small increases in system softirq CPU time and iowait on host (0.5-1.5s windows).
- perf/ftrace: userland trace showed our runtime's batch loop entering a wait state (epoll_wait) and then resuming after a 30-120ms window; immediately preceding the wait there was a burst of ksoftirqd activity and rtnetlink/NAPI handling.
- tcpdump & pkt capture: bursts of ACKs and small packets from GPU telemetry and KMS heartbeats correlated with timing of the stalls.
- nvprof / nvidia-smi dmon: GPU kernels showed expected execution but with occasional gaps where host-side post-processing wasn't feeding new batches timely (NVTX ranges aligned).
- strace on runtime IO thread: observed occasional scheduling latency on epoll_ctl/epoll_wait wake-ups.

Root cause hypothesis (synthesis):
- On affected hosts we had aggressive NIC interrupt coalescing parameters (rx-usecs ~ 2000 us) configured by the vendor image to reduce CPU interrupts at low rates. Under our mixed-tenant fluctuating traffic pattern that caused network events to be coalesced into bursts.
- A burst of coalesced net interrupts caused NAPI/softirq processing to run for tens of milliseconds. On machines with high CPU utilization and default CFS scheduler settings, ksoftirqd contention bumped our runtime IO threads off the CPU for short windows.
- Our runtime’s batching logic has tight timing thresholds: if the IO thread misses a wakeup, the batch is flushed later, or downstream worker threads idle while waiting for the next batch, producing the observed 20–200ms service-time increase for affected requests.
- Compounding factor: system-level CPU isolation/cgroup config placed runtime IO threads on non-isolated CPUs so they were preemptible by ksoftirqd and IRQ handling.

Why other hypotheses were deprioritized:
- GPU driver stalls (e.g., DMA faults): ruled out — no GPU errors in dmesg, no nvml memory anomalies, consistent kernel durations when executed.
- NVMe/PCIe link down/up: no link fluctuation logs; SMART and iostat normal.
- kV cache repop storms: not aligned with traces — kV repop showed smaller, longer tail patterns (seconds) vs short bursts we saw here.

Repro steps (staging harness):
- Use a low-QPS streaming generator to emulate customer stream patterns (cmds available in /infra/testing/stream-gen).
- Set NIC coalescing to high: ethtool -C eth0 rx-usecs 2000 tx-usecs 2000
- Run: ./serve-runtime --model-route=llama-q4 --max-batch-ms=4 --io-cpu-affinity=default
- Observe: collect perf/ftrace: perf record -e sched:sched_wakeup,sched_switch -a -g -- sleep 60
- Use: sudo ./scripts/collect-host-profiles.sh --nvml --ftrace --tcpdump --output /tmp/prof
- Expected: reproduce 30-150ms epoll latency windows and corresponding 99p increase.

Mitigations deployed (short-term / hotfix):
1) Host NIC tuning: reduce rx-usecs to 250 and enable adaptive-coalesce where available. Rationale: reduce coalescing latency so packet processing becomes more continuous and less bursty.
2) Runtime IO thread scheduler hints: set SCHED_BATCH -> SCHED_FIFO 80 or set cpu-affinity to isolated CPU cores (using cpuset) for IO and runtime main threads on dedicated cores. Rationale: avoid preemption by ksoftirqd and reduce wakeup jitter.
3) Runtime change (hotfix PR #2146): add micro-wakeup backstop to epoll_wait path — if epoll_wait takes >10ms, proactively poll for new work for a short window. This is a defensive measure so a missed wakeup doesn't translate into a full batch-timing miss.

Validation and results:
- Canary (20 nodes) with synthetic streaming workload (QPS 2 per node, average tokens per request 600):
  - Baseline 99p: 420ms
  - After host NIC tuning only: 99p -> 280ms (partial improvement)
  - After adding CPU-affinity for IO threads: 99p -> 230ms
  - After hotfix PR (#2146) on top of the above: 99p -> 210ms
  - CPU cost: small increase in system CPU (2–3%) on tuned nodes; acceptable tradeoff for SLO.
- Production rollout: 12% of nodes were targeted first (same SKU); after 72 hours, percentage of affected hosts dropped below noise; global 99p for the model group improved by ~40%.

Notes on measurements and graphs (appendix pointers):
- Attached flamegraph snapshots in the Confluence page show the epoll_wait -> sched switch path, aligned to NVTX ranges.
- Perf counters: context-switches/kmalloc/free spikes matched softirq bursts.
- Packet timing: tcpdump histograms show aggregated ACK bursts with ~1.8–2.2ms spacing within bursts when coalescing was enabled; after tuning spacing became more uniform.

Action items (short-term):
- Roll NIC coalescing adjustments to all prod g7x-large pools. (Owner: InfraOps, ETA: 2026-01-20)
- Merge hotfix PR #2146 and release new runtime binary with feature flag. (Owner: Serving-runtime eng, ETA: 2026-01-19)
- Add placement rule to ensure IO threads are bound to isolated CPUs for latency-sensitive workloads. (Owner: Platform-eng, ETA: 2026-02-01)
- Update runbooks: include NIC coalescing diagnostic steps, and a new 'missed-wakeup' check in our SRE incident triage. (Owner: Eng-SRE, ETA: 2026-01-25)

Action items (longer-term / follow-ups):
- Evaluate host image defaults: request vendor to change rx-usecs default for our inference image families. (Owner: InfraOps)
- Investigate moving critical runtime IO handling into an NAPI-friendly kernel bypass (e.g., using AF_XDP) to eliminate softirq path variability. (Owner: Eng-serving-runtime research)
- Add observability metric: epoll-wakeup-latency histogram emitted by runtime to correlate with SLO in real-time. (Owner: DevEx)
- Conduct a controlled experiment on other instance SKUs (g7x-medium, dedicated pools) to validate kernel scheduling interactions generalize. (Owner: Performance team)

Appendix A — Quick commands used during investigation:
- collect NVTX timeline: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./samples/timeline-record --out /tmp/tl.json
- nvidia monitor: nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1
- perf: sudo perf record -e sched:sched_switch -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 60; sudo perf script -i /tmp/perf.data | ./scripts/stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./scripts/flamegraph.pl > /tmp/flame.svg
- ethtool inspect: ethtool -c eth0
- ftrace snapshot: echo function > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/current_tracer; echo 1 > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/tracing_on; cat /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/trace > /tmp/trace

Appendix B — Notes to self / open questions:
- Is adaptive-coalesce stable across our cloud provider's NIC drivers? A couple of hosts showed different behavior; need to inventory NIC driver versions.
- Should we add a conservative default to the runtime to always prefer local CPU-affinity hints in images provided to Dedicated customers?
- Can we surface the epoll-wakeup-latency metric into Console per-route dashboards? This will help customers debug similar low-qps streaming issues without opening a ticket.

Customer communication draft (for CS):
- Short: "We identified intermittent host-level network interrupt coalescing interacting with the Linux scheduler that caused short stalls in the inference process and increased tail latency for some streaming workloads. We deployed mitigations (NIC tuning + runtime scheduling hints + small runtime backstop) that reduced 99p latency by ~50% for affected flows. We're rolling to all hosts and will monitor continuity."
- Longer: include list of affected SKUs, ETA for full rollout, mitigation details, and suggested temporary client-side retries/timeouts.

End of doc.
